count_semantics: Eight linked research entries, including qualifications and one newly noticed timing difference; not eight independent witnesses or proven conspiracies.

findings.title: A reported hold note and unanswered follow-up do not identify the original decision-maker
findings.claim_type: Source-supported review finding; original messages unacquired
findings.observation: CIA physical p.78 / printed p.53 reports a January 5, 2000 FBI detailee draft CIR addressed to FBI Headquarters and the New York Field Office, a targeting analyst's afternoon note attributing a hold instruction to the station's CIA-officer deputy chief, and a January 13 Lotus Note asking whether the draft should be remade. The review found no reply. DOJ III.A.4 separately reports the attributed note and unanswered mid-January inquiry.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: The attribution in the analyst's note is not an acquired direct order, recording or authenticated identity of the actual decision-maker.
CIA pp.78 and80 / printed pp.53 and55 and DOJ III.A.4 describe access by FBI detailees. Failure to disseminate the formal CIR does not mean no FBI employee could access the underlying information.
Both reviews report failed formal dissemination. Repetition through related oversight reviews is not another independent contemporaneous witness.
findings.next_test: Obtain the native CIR, attributed hold annotation/version history, January 13 Lotus Note and any reply, release-authority records, access audits and actual intended-recipient delivery trail. Preserve pseudonyms and redactions; do not guess a real identity.
findings.limit: The reports establish a documented non-dissemination/hold inquiry, not an attack-purpose or higher-level authorization finding.

findings.title: SCALEC 134684 is an identifiable internal delivery claim with unverified external receipt
findings.claim_type: Source-supported cable identifier and unresolved delivery question
findings.observation: CIA physical p.79 / printed p.54 and its Appendix F5.b-1 physical p.108 / printed p.83 identify SCALEC 134684, dated January 5, 2000, as an internal cable claiming the travel documents had been passed to the FBI. Footnote14 says ALEC is the station's cable cite. The review could not identify the recipient or method, or confirm or refute successful delivery. It found no evidence of a later receipt check.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: The claimed informal passage is distinct from the formal draft CIR that was not disseminated. One must not be silently substituted for the other.

DOJ III.A.6 and III.A.8.b describe an internal operational cable without recipient/method information, unable to corroborate the asserted passage. DOJ's assessment of the contemporary briefings is more negative than merely repeating the claim.
CIA p.77 / printed p.52 describes formal and informal channels in practice. That supplies an alternative route to investigate, not proof that this delivery succeeded.
findings.additional_context: CIA physical p.81 / printed p.56 reports a January20 note saying the FBI had been kept abreast. It also says the review had no information of further communication with the FBI outside the station's detailees after January6. This is another review-described assertion and scope limit, not the acquired original January20 email.
findings.next_test: Recover the original SCALEC 134684 with attachments, routing/dissemination fields and referenced handoff; compare recipient-side incoming logs, contemporaneous briefing notes and any January 20 follow-up. No January 20 original was recovered here.
findings.limit: A recorded assertion of delivery is not a receipt. The original cable was not acquired; no deliberate false entry is established.

findings.title: DUCS database deletion, a retention instruction and a surviving Lotus copy are different preservation events
findings.claim_type: Source-supported preservation lead; deletion purpose and exact scope unverified
findings.observation: CIA physical p.78 / printed p.53 footnote13 says CTC deleted its DUCS database in late 2002 when DUCS was decommissioned. It expressly says the review did not know when this particular draft cable was ultimately deleted. The copy obtained in January 2004 was the version preserved in the January 13, 2000 Lotus Note.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: The same page reports mid-February instructions to delete other dead cables while specifically retaining this draft CIR; DOJ III.A.4 likewise reports that retention request. Those instructions do not establish what was ultimately retained or migrated.

Database deletion is a reported event in a later review, not an acquired native deletion log. The surviving email copy rules out a claim that no copy survived, but does not establish completeness of all versions, attachments, backups or audits.
Decommissioning is the reported context. It does not itself establish lawful retention compliance, improper destruction or an intent to obstruct oversight.
findings.next_test: Obtain DUCS decommissioning, migration, retention schedules/holds, backups and deletion/audit records; join them to the draft's versions, the mid-February retain instruction and the surviving Lotus attachment.
findings.limit: No finding that every copy was destroyed, that this draft was selectively targeted, or that deletion concealed attack involvement.

findings.title: CIA January and DOJ February 2004 discovery accounts require a version-and-recipient chronology
findings.claim_type: Attributable oversight chronology with unresolved source-version join
findings.observation: CIA physical p.78 / printed p.53 says its OIG obtained the Lotus-preserved draft only in January 2004. DOJ Chapter V II.1 says it noticed a previously undisclosed CIR title in February 2004 while reviewing a list of documents accessed by FBI employees at CIA; it also says CIA OIG had not previously obtained the document in connection with its review. DOJ says the belated discovery required more interviews/documents and delayed completion.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: Preserve CIA's January date, DOJ's February date and DOJ's statement about CIA's previous acquisition together. The version, exact acquisition time and inter-review transmission are not joined by native receipts.

Different agencies, copies and discovery/receipt events could matter, but that is an untested possibility, not a reconciliation adopted here. Neither an established contradiction about one identical receipt nor a resolved non-conflict is claimed.

DOJ II.1 says it lacked independent CIA database access and initially could review but not retain copies of certain records. That is a documented completeness constraint, not proof of coordinated concealment.
findings.next_test: Recover dated CIA/DOJ OIG requests, search and access lists, acquisition receipts, interview schedules, version/attachment hashes and cross-review production records for January–February 2004.
findings.limit: The delay and search limitation are real reported oversight issues. The examined records do not identify the cause of delayed discovery or prove coordinated nonproduction.

findings.title: A formatting explanation in the CIA summary is qualified by its detailed account and DOJ's assessment
findings.observation: CIA physical p.17 / printed p.xv says the message was apparently not sent because it was in the wrong format or needed editing. CIA physical p.79 / printed p.54 attributes major-editing concerns to an officer's speculation on reviewing a copy in early February 2004, after the account of participants' inability to recall the draft. DOJ III.A.8.a instead describes the information as documented in the appropriate format and says it could not determine why the CIR was not disseminated.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: All three source formulations remain side by side: apparent formatting/editing explanation, retrospective editing speculation, and DOJ's appropriate-format/unknown-reason assessment.
No contemporaneous format rejection, editing instruction, revised draft or release decision was acquired. A later suggested reason cannot be silently promoted into the established January 2000 cause.

The wording difference does not itself establish a consciously false summary. Formatting, classification sanitization, release authority and delivery are separate questions for the original workflow records.
findings.next_test: Recover contemporaneous version histories, classification/editing reviews, release instructions and any rejection/rework record; compare the source basis used for the executive summary and detailed passage.
findings.limit: A source-backed question about the asserted explanation and its evidentiary basis; not a finding of deliberate falsification or attack-purpose withholding.

findings.title: No accountability recommendation on uncertain January passage is not general exoneration
findings.claim_type: Source-scope qualification and distinct affirmative failure findings
findings.observation: CIA physical pp.105–106 / printed pp.80–81 makes no accountability recommendation concerning January informal passage because it could neither confirm nor refute that passage. The same discussion reports a separate March 2000 failure to tell the FBI about Hazmi's US-bound departure and later missed opportunities. Page105 also recommends an Accountability Board assessment of systemic watchlisting management.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: Uncertainty about one delivery issue is retained alongside affirmative findings on other failures; it is not recast as proof all conduct was proper.

The report's findings are not the final disposition of a later Accountability Board, discipline decision, criminal inquiry or historical-cause adjudication. Those later outcomes were not established in this pass.
DOJ's own accountability assessment distinguishes CIA responsibility, FBI detailee initiative and inadequate further follow-up. Those statements do not identify a single attack-motivated actor.

DOJ IV.D's introductory assessment says none of the evaluated FBI employees committed misconduct, although several performed below what they should have. It expressly leaves CIA personnel accountability to CIA OIG. Preserve that adverse-to-misconduct finding with the performance criticisms; do not extend it to every CIA action.
findings.next_test: Obtain the underlying March cables/access audits, action logs and the issue-specific accountability referral/response and final board or management dispositions. Do not infer an actual sanction from a recommendation.
findings.limit: Supports an accountability inquiry, not a final finding of conspiracy, exoneration, criminal intent or WTC 7 involvement.

findings.title: The December 16, 2003 redacted MFR is a bounded record lead, not an authenticated real-name or CIR join
findings.claim_type: Official-host source recovery and limited catalog association
findings.observation: The independently re-fetched NARA media PDF has four physical pages and matches the held copy byte-for-byte. Page1 gives a December16,2003 interview, December17 preparation, Team4, and FBI-headquarters location; it says the memorandum is not verbatim and is organized by subject. The official MFR index lists NAID2610319, [FBI Employee #2], FBI affiliation, December16,2003, four pages, redacted, box13.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: These visible attributes are consistent with the index entry, but the catalog's item-to-media asset crosswalk was not retrieved. The filename/index association is not presented as a completed metadata-level join.

All four visible pages were independently read. The subject's identity and major ALEC/pre-9/11 passages remain redacted. Visible text does not establish this subject authored, held or received the January 2000 CIR.
No secondary site's real-name identification is adopted, and the redacted subject is not treated as an additional identified witness to the hold.

source_refs.locator: NAID2610319 row; [FBI Employee #2], 12/16/2003, four pages, R, box13

findings.next_test: Obtain the complete NARA catalog item/object mapping and authorized declassified underlying interview records. Test any claimed CIR/identity connection with explicit records rather than redaction reconstruction.
findings.limit: The official-host PDF is verified as the bytes examined; the visible text supplies no direct proof of the proposed CIR decision chain or a named individual's participation.

findings.title: Five-day, eight-day and January 13 follow-up descriptions remain distinct
findings.claim_type: Low-weight timing-description discrepancy noticed during this check
findings.observation: DOJ Chapter V IV.D.1 says the drafter inquired again five days later. Its III.A.4 narrative says that as of eight days later the CIR was still undispatched and describes a mid-January email; III.A.8.a says a week later. CIA physical p.78 / printed p.53 explicitly dates the draft January5 and the Lotus follow-up January13,2000.
conflicting_or_qualifying_records: The exact source phrases five days later, eight days later, a week later, and the January5/January13 dates are preserved. Simple subtraction of the named calendar dates gives eight days; it does not authenticate which underlying email the other summaries describe.
An approximation, a different reference point, another communication or an editorial error are untested possibilities. No date is corrected or selected as controlling.
The differing elapsed-time descriptions do not remove the reviews' shared finding that the formal CIR was not sent or establish deliberate alteration of the record.
findings.next_test: Obtain the native dated email(s), attachment versions, audit and response records, and compare the report's drafting/citation history. Keep separate any distinct follow-up events.
findings.limit: A documentary precision lead with little independent bearing on motive or attack participation; it must not inflate the count of independent evidence chains.
